title: protocol.json.method
description: Which method manifest (methods/*.json) governs this review, recorded once at protocol time. Read by tools/method.py. Absence of this whole block (a legacy protocol.json predating this schema) means "systematic_review", recorded=false -- see docs/PLAN.md M1's migration path, not an error. The `routing`/`signed_at`/`signed_by` fields (docs/PLAN.md M2; references/docs/design/multi-method-consensus.md §2.3) are only written once /litreview-init's Step 0.5 routing interview exists; a protocol.json written before that (or under M1) carries only `id` and, optionally, `recorded` -- every M2 field is optional for exactly that reason.

id.description: Must match a methods/<id>.json manifest's own "id" field -- tools/method.py checks this at resolve time, not this schema (the set of shipped methods changes across milestones).

recorded.description: True when a reviewer (or /litreview-init's routing, from docs/PLAN.md M2 onward) actually chose this method before the first protocol-driven run. tools/method.py sets this false only for its own defaulted resolution when the block is absent entirely -- never hand-set false in a real protocol.json.

version.description: The methods/<id>.json manifest's own "version" at the moment this review recorded it -- lets label_gate.py and /litreview-status notice the manifest has moved on since routing, without forcing a re-route.

synthesis_family.description: Set by routing rows R6e/R6f (tools/route.py) when the chosen method is systematic_review and the goal is an answerable comparison; null for methods that never pool (reconnaissance, scoping_review, systematic_mapping_study). Distinct from synthesis_plan.json's own synthesis_family, which review-protocol writes at G-Protocol once this value has narrowed the plan elicitation to pairwise_iv.

profile_flags.description: Profiles offered at routing (R7) and accepted by the reviewer, e.g. ["rapid"], ["single_reviewer"]. Not method choices -- label_gate.py reads these to compute e.g. the rapid label from shortcuts[], never from calendar time.

modes.description: Maintenance modes layered over the chosen method, e.g. ["living"] when R1 resolves to LIVING(base). A mode, unlike a method, has no manifest of its own.

pack.description: R9 pack resolution result (tools/route.py resolve_pack()) -- a packs/<id>.json field pack, or null until packs ship (docs/PLAN.md M3).

output_profiles.description: Extra deliverables the chosen method produces beyond its default output, e.g. ["prior_work_check", "background_section"] for reconnaissance (R3).

table_version.description: methods/_routing.json's own "table_version" at the moment this review was routed -- the audit trail for which rule set produced this recommendation.

answers.description: The Q1-Q6 answers elicited by /litreview-init Step 0.5 (§2.1), verbatim, as passed to tools.route.decide(). Schema-free here -- the answer vocabulary is owned by the routing table and its reference documentation, not duplicated into this schema.

q0.description: The computed-after-Q1 orienting run and its human judgement: {raw_files[], human_judgement, registry_lookup: {date, result, url} | null}. Required for the systematic_review label's PROSPERO/OSF-lookup conduct-floor check (label_gate.py); null only before Q0 has run.

recommended_id.description: What tools.route.decide() recommended -- a method id, or a refused target's name (e.g. "meta_aggregation") when the row resolved to a refusal the reviewer then routed around by hand.

chosen_id.description: What the reviewer actually confirmed at G-Route (the first human gate) -- equal to recommended_id unless overridden (R10).

override_reason.description: Required when chosen_id != recommended_id; null otherwise. The label is still computed from recorded conduct regardless of this override.

fallback_reason.description: Set when the routing table itself fell down the claims ladder (refused, or R7's afternoon-and-answer override) rather than the reviewer overriding by hand. Printed verbatim in the manuscript's Methods -- never paraphrased.

signed_at.description: When the reviewer confirmed chosen_id at G-Route. Distinct from synthesis_plan.json's own signed_at and protocol.json's overall protocol sign-off.

signed_by.description: Reviewer id/name confirming the routing choice, for the audit trail label_gate.py's conduct-floor checks read.
